principles.statement: Use Vietnamese L1 evidence as a prior for what to test, never as proof that an individual learner has a problem.
Let observed learner evidence override Vietnamese population priors immediately when the learner succeeds or fails consistently under valid probes.

For pronunciation, prioritize Vietnamese-risk targets by intelligibility, lexical or grammatical contrast value, frequency, learner failure and learnability rather than by distance from a native accent.
Keep pronunciation perception and production evidence separate; do not infer that producing a contrast proves reliable recognition of it in speech or vice versa.
Probe English prominence with both pitch and timing/context cues because Vietnamese learners may initially over-rely on tonal strategies.
Stage coda and cluster work from communicatively consequential, learnable contrasts toward more complex clusters; do not make native-like complex-cluster production a blanket beginner gate.
When a Vietnamese learner knows a written word but misses it in audio, route first to phonological decoding or chunk-boundary diagnosis before adding more vocabulary explanation.
Include short chunk-level listening probes that can distinguish sound confusion, deletion, insertion or boundary failure from meaning failure.
Treat collocations and useful formulaic sequences as first-class lexical targets for Vietnamese learners; component-word knowledge is insufficient evidence of chunk knowledge.
Record L1-L2 congruency as a possible chunk-difficulty feature and use Vietnamese contrast or translation selectively when it helps establish a non-congruent form-meaning mapping, then fade it.

For grammar, give early diagnostic attention to meaning-bearing features weakly or differently marked in Vietnamese, including articles, number morphology, tense/aspect, agreement and copular constructions, but teach them through meaning-linked constructions rather than error-rule lists.
Do not convert written Vietnamese learner error frequencies directly into spoken-curriculum priorities; confirm comprehension and production difficulty in the relevant modality and capability.
Store Vietnamese-specific risk priors separately from learner evidence so the model can distinguish population-informed suspicion from demonstrated individual need.
Do not infer Vietnamese dialect or regional speech patterns from nationality alone; collect dialect information only when useful and keep it lower-confidence until behavior confirms relevance.
Teach pragmatic variation through concrete relationships and situations rather than presenting one English norm or one Vietnamese norm as universally correct.
Keep all Vietnamese-specific target priorities, probe thresholds, dialect modifiers and remediation doses falsifiable until EXP-019 validates them with Nếp’s near-A0/A1 population.
